chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Mālik al-Juhanī, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام):
His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: “And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby, and whomever it reaches.”
He said: “Whoever it reaches such that he is to be an Imam from the progeny of Muḥammad, then he warns by the Qur'an just as the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) warned by it.”

key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله, from whom the Imam is identified
key_terms.إِمَامًا: an Imam; the divinely designated leader from the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.الْقُرْآنُ: the divine revelation by which warning and guidance are conveyed
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, whose mode of warning by the Qur'an the Imam continues
key_terms.لِأُنْذِرَكُمْ: to warn you; the Qur'an's function of admonition and caution
key_terms.وَمَنْ بَلَغَ: and whomever it reaches; interpreted here with reference to the one who attains the station of Imamate

ai.seo_question: How do the Imams from آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ continue the Qur'anic mission of warning mentioned in Qur'an 6:19?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse as extending the function of warning by the Qur'an to the Imam from the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله. It presents the Imam as carrying forward the Qur'anic mission of guidance and warning after the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
